TenkaCloud / Open-source practice and competition platform

Cloud and security,learned by doing.

TenkaCloud is an open-source platform for hands-on cloud and security exercises and competitions. Organizers host events locally or on AWS, working with problems, teams, submissions, scoring and rankings.

Why hands-on practice

Bridge knowing and doing.

Security matters. But where do you start? Experienced people are scarce and costly. Put textbook knowledge to work in a safe exercise, see what happens, and learn from the result.

  1. Choose a problem

    Organizers choose problems for their learners and goals: basic games, Challenges or Battles.

  2. Try it hands-on

    Work with a supported simulator or real environment, as appropriate for the problem. Check its guide for access requirements and costs.

  3. Check the result

    Submit answers or checkpoints, then review scoring, hints and score changes. Try again to check your understanding.

One example of the learning approach

See what happens. Act. Compare the result.

Problems vary with the organizer and learning goal. This in-development authorization bug illustrates one approach: understand the impact, act, and verify the fix.

In-development example: explore how a data leak happens

Experience in development · Three minutes is a target

Data breaches make the news. How do they happen?

Experience a security incident in three minutes.

Understand how data leaks, then practice stopping it.

The first challenge is in development. Someone else’s fictional customer data is exposed. Fix the settings, then check that others cannot read it while its owner still can. Completion time is unverified; this challenge is not playable yet.

CASE 001 / BROKEN ACCESS CONTROL

One changed ID. One broken boundary.

Local illustration · All data is fictional · Not a scored challenge

Fictional customer dataID 1042
200 OK Your information is visible. Expected behavior. Someone else’s information is visible. Authorization is missing. No one else’s data is returned. The boundary holds.
01 / REQUEST

You’re signed in.
Are you safe?

Your page requests data for ID 1042. Authentication checks who you are. Authorization checks whose data you may read. Those are different questions.

Change just one ID ↓
02 / EXPOSURE

Change the ID.
See someone else’s data.

1042 → 1043. Without an ownership check, the server returns another person’s fictional information. Hiding the URL will not stop this leak.

Behind that response is someone’s personal information. First, feel the impact.

03 / CONTAINMENT

Stop the leak.
Keep the service running.

On the server, compare the signed-in user with the data owner. Your data: 200. Someone else’s: 403. Blocking everyone is not a correct fix. Switch between the two IDs to verify both.

session.userId === record.ownerId

This authorization challenge is in development and is not available in the cloud. The illustration above has no scoring. Three minutes is a target; first-run completion time has not been measured.

Who it's for

Build cloud capability across the org.

For Cloud Enablement (CCoE), Platform / SRE, and Security teams that need hands-on AWS training — without rebuilding the event platform. Environment provisioning, login, scoring, and progress tracking — all in one screen.

Cloud Enablement / CCoE

Run training events multiple times a year.

New-grad onboarding, internalization programs, cross-team AWS drills — run them multiple times a year on the same platform. Move from one-off workshops to a planned annual program.

Contact form (Google sign-in required) ›
Platform / SRE

Design drills from one screen.

Manage events, teams, problems and scores in shared consoles. Local and AWS hosting use different runtimes. Check the organizer guide for each problem’s access conditions and verification status.

Operator guide ›
Engineers / individual learners

Sharpen on the real thing.

An open-source platform for learning through competitions. Communities and schools can host locally; AWS exercises use cloud hosting. The OSS license is free; cloud resources are billed separately.

Author a problem ›
Enterprise use cases

Turn security training into a game.

Play → Reflect → Try again

Review scores and outcomes, then try what you learned in another exercise. We aim to help knowledge stick through practice that teams want to repeat.

All employees / non-engineers

Learn to spot deception by doing.

Turn phishing, social engineering and other situations your company could face into problems, and share what teams notice as they solve them. Participants join from a browser; they do not install TenkaCloud.

New engineers

Start simple. Put it into practice.

Start with a short Challenge: read the problem and hints, then submit an answer. Organizers can choose topics for their learners, including investigation and hands-on environment tasks.

SRE / SOC

Drill incident response.

Use outage-response and attack/defense Battle problems to practice judging a situation and acting as a team. The score timeline shows where teams got stuck.

Internal events

A cross-team CTF, in-house.

Manage events, teams, problems and scores from the organizer console, and give each team its own key or invitation link. The scoreboard shares rankings with everyone.

Operator guide ›
Internal network

Host from a single PC.

Local hosting runs on SQLite and needs no AWS account. Participants can join from other devices over the LAN or Tailscale. Check the startup guide for connection and Docker problem requirements.

Startup guide ›
Checking retention

Repeat rounds to check retention.

Run the same or similar problems again after some time, and compare team scores and solve status with the previous round. Training does not end after one session.

Read the book

The whole method, in one book.

Build a local Challenge, an AWS Challenge, and an AWS Battle in increasing order of difficulty, then run them as a competition several teams can play. It is written around TenkaCloud, but reading it needs neither an AWS account nor a TenkaCloud install. Available in English and Japanese.

Getting started and costs

Host it yourself, or get operational help.

TenkaCloud is Apache-2.0 open source. The license, cloud resource costs and operated-event service fees are separate. Use the guides to host it yourself, or review the scope and pricing if you want help with design and event operations.

Operated-event scope, pricing and contact
Commercial offerings

Three productized offerings — formally documented.

The OSS platform stays free under Apache 2.0. For organizations that want setup, live operations, or a program run for them, we offer three productized packages. Each has a fixed shape — scope, deliverables, exclusions, delivery model.

Hosted Event

One operated drill, end to end.

A 1-day cloud drill on the public OSS catalog, run by us. Event design, deploy into your AWS account, dry run, live facilitation, post-event report. Per-event fixed price.

Annual Arena

A 12-month program.

An annual contract of 4 operated events per year for one org: learning paths curated from the public problem catalog (beginner → advanced). Original problem development is not included in this package.

CCoE Enablement (add-on)

Advisory, sold separately.

A monthly retainer for operating-model / training-roadmap work. Never bundled into the two offerings above, so events stay productized. If you want both, that is two line items.
